The organ that pumps blood is the heart.

The provided text describes a public transportation website that uses graphical formats for real-time schedules without accompanying text descriptions. This design choice creates significant accessibility barriers, particularly for individuals who rely on screen readers. Screen readers cannot interpret visual data such as charts, graphs, or images unless they are accompanied by alternative text (alt text) or detailed textual descriptions. Without these descriptions, users with visual impairments are unable to access critical information about bus and train schedules, effectively excluding them from using the service. To improve accessibility, the website should provide text-based alternatives for all graphical content, ensuring that schedule information is available in a format compatible with assistive technologies. Additionally, following WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) standards would involve ensuring that all non-text content has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose.
